summary: Forest Service ground cabin built in 1916 on Parkview Mountain's summit; unused as a lookout since 1948, still standing, and condition is poor-fair per a 2019 report.

facts.design: Ground cabin with concrete walls and a wood frame
facts.status_note: Standing on the summit but not used since 1948. A 2019 report rates the exterior poor to fair.

access.note: Reached on foot by hiking up from Willow Creek Pass per 2008 and 2022 accounts; no closure found in sources. Official Forest Service access status was not verified, and the cab's condition is poor to fair.

visit.trail_note: Hike from Willow Creek Pass on Colorado 125, or drive part way on primitive roads (SummitPost). A 2008 Denver Post hike starts at a small parking area 0.3 miles south of the pass on Forest Service Road 266.1H.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Routt National Forest

events.note: Ground cabin built by the Forest Service; NHLR calls it the groundhouse built in 1916.
A November 1919 Routt County Sentinel item, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says an officer was stationed on the peak through dry summer periods.
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: August 13, 2003.
SummitPost describes the cabin as recently restored to usable condition and links a 2007 photo showing restoration. The text itself is undated.
A 2008 Denver Post article says the building still served as a radio repeater station for firefighters.
A 2019 report rates the exterior poor to fair and says it has had no maintenance for a long time.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR header and Denver Post give 12,296 ft (3,748 m). The NHLR description says 12,225 ft. The story reports the 12,296 figure and notes the mismatch.
NHLR says it has not been used since 1948 and uses past tense for the repeater. A 2008 Denver Post article says it still serves as a repeater station. The story reports both and does not settle it.
NHLR's 2019 report rates the exterior poor to fair with no recent maintenance. SummitPost says it was recently restored, with no date. A 2007 photo link is the only dated restoration clue.

notes_for_editor: The brief's events omitted the 1916 build and the 1948 end of use; those are added here as events, not corrections. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced by a 'public' level based on visitor accounts and the absence of a closure in the sources. Official Forest Service access status was not checked, so please verify before publication. The 2019 condition note from NHLR conflicts with the SummitPost restoration claim. The 1919 newspaper item is quoted second-hand on Forest Lookouts. height_m is omitted because the sources give no tower height. No new photo URLs were added.
